label: local-substitute
scope: Review of the optional lazy 3D lighting scene (LightingScene.tsx) in headless Chromium with software WebGL (swiftshader) against isolated native servers and a synthetic tenant: not a user GPU, not assistive technology.
findings: axe: aria-prohibited-attr (serious) on the canvas wrapper, which carried aria-label without a role. Fixed with role="img"; desktop, portrait and reduced-motion axe runs now report zero violations. (The 2026-11-02 accessibility evidence ran with reduced motion, so it never rendered the canvas.)

Keyboard: the canvas is not a tab stop and OrbitControls is pointer-only. Accepted: orbiting conveys no information and the only functional control, the three-way temperature radio group, is keyboard operable (arrow keys change the selection, focus outline 3px, Tab leaves the scene).
Reduced motion: no canvas is created; the static fallback is shown.
Capture privacy: no credential, token, email or phone pattern in the page text; the scene is labelled 'Illustrative 3D scene'.

performance.script_requests: 40 dev-server script requests (unbundled; sizes not representative, see production_build)

production_build.note: Three.js and react-three-fiber are in the lazy LightingScene chunk, not the entry chunk; the 934 kB scene chunk exceeds Vite's 700 kB warning threshold (it is lazy, so it does not load with the entry chunk); the 616 kB entry chunk is under it.

limits: Timings come from the Vite dev server in a headless browser; a production-build timing on real hardware is not measured.
Idle frames (123 in 2 s on this software renderer) were measured by an unrelated requestAnimationFrame counter, so they do not prove frameloop="demand" stops rendering.
No human keyboard or screen-reader session.
